abbott_smith_html:
κατ-αισχύνω
[in LXX chiefly for בּוּשׁ ;]
to disgrace, dishonour, put to shame: with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.11:4-5; with accusative of person(s), 1Co.1:27 11:22; pass., to be ashamed: Luk.13:17, 2Co.7:14 9:4, 1Pe.3:16; as in LXX (Psa.22:6 25:2-3, al.), of unfulfilled hopes: Rom.5:5; pass., Rom.9:33 10:11, 1Pe.2:6" (LXX) .†
(AS)

strongs_1890.strongs_def: to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush

occurrences.bsb: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.
occurrences.kjv: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

occurrences.bsb: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.
occurrences.kjv: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.

occurrences.bsb: as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
occurrences.kjv: As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

occurrences.bsb: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
occurrences.kjv: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

occurrences.bsb: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
occurrences.kjv: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;

occurrences.bsb: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
occurrences.kjv: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonoureth his head.

occurrences.bsb: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.
occurrences.kjv: But every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with her head uncovered dishonoureth her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven.

occurrences.bsb: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!
occurrences.kjv: What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.

occurrences.bsb: Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.
occurrences.kjv: For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth.

occurrences.bsb: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.
occurrences.kjv: Lest haply if they of Macedonia come with me, and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, ye) should be ashamed in this same confident boasting.

occurrences.bsb: For it stands in Scripture: “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
occurrences.kjv: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.

occurrences.bsb: keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.
occurrences.kjv: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.
